NFL.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
NFL.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). No Week 9 game or the BUF-MIN game disagrees with the Vegas favorite, so no new cases.
NFL.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

NFL.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
NFL.evidence: Before Week 9, 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick. Week 9 split: TB-CHI (gap 5.0) lost, CIN-ATL (gap 4.9) won. That makes it 1 of 7 at best. The Week 9 gap-4.2 game JAX-BAL won. Overall the over/under is 28-24.
NFL.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

NFL.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
NFL.evidence: In 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason. The new miss, GB-NE, came from turnovers (NE 4, GB 0). Week 9 blowouts split: KC-NYJ and LV-SF came from finishing drives and turnovers, while HOU-LAC, CIN-ATL and most of JAX-BAL had no stat explanation.
NFL.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

NFL.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
NFL.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 18 against 7.2 expected (-5.54 units). Big-game picks are 11 of 35 against 11.5 expected (-10.49 units). Combined, 16 of 53 against 18.7 expected. The big-game hit rate is now near expectation, so most of its unit loss comes from prices. The underdog gap is about 2 hits. Milestone picks are 30 of 39 against 29.1 expected (-3.41 units).
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

NFL.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
NFL.evidence: 11 of 23 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.2 expected, at -2.00 units. The gap to expectation has shrunk from 2 hits to about 1. This week's Under 45.5 sits only 0.4 points over break-even.
NFL.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

NFL.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
NFL.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model against 8.9 for Vegas over 55 graded games. The model is 24-30-1 against the spread. Winners are 38 of 54 (70%). Week 9 went 5-8 against the spread.
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

NFL.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
NFL.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts (on IR); DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again; WAS won 27-10 against the model's WAS by 3.3 (Vegas -6). This week the brief lists Kyler Murray for MIN, but he is out and Carson Wentz starts. The model has MIN at 46% against Vegas 36%. That is 3 known cases, well under 20.
NFL.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

NFL.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
NFL.evidence: 15 of 23 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 16.9 expected, at -3.77 units. The shortfall is about 2 hits. Overall winners are 38 of 54 (70%), so the model's winner calls look better than its pick-list results.
NFL.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up, and the model's totals picks overall have lost more than they won.
College.evidence: Weeks 8-9: over hit in 11 of 29 such games. Week 10 (40 results shown): 5 of 10 (UCF-Kansas, Oregon-Ohio State, Delaware-Kennesaw State, Tulsa-Tulane, North Carolina-UConn went over; Arizona State-Colorado, Air Force-Army, Notre Dame-Miami, Vanderbilt-Mississippi State, Duke-NC State did not). Combined 16 of 39 (41%). Season totals picks are 105-125 (46%); 14-25 in the Week 10 results shown.
College.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads.
College.evidence: Week 10, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, finishing drives 5, turnovers 4, nothing stood out 2, defensive/return touchdowns 1. Week 9 had efficiency first in 7 of 26; Week 8 in 15 of 25. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
College.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

College.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, results are mixed to poor.
College.evidence: About 4 of 12 right overall. The only disagreement in the Week 10 results shown was Tulane (model by 3.0, Vegas Tulsa -3); Tulsa won 60-10. Arizona State at UCF (model Arizona State by 0.5, Vegas UCF -3.5) is the open case this week. Sample is small.
College.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

College.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
College.evidence: Season: 12 of 30 hit against 15.3 expected, at -7.09 units (was 8 of 22 last run, so 4 of 8 this week). The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five picks this week.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
College.evidence: Season: 10 of 29 hit against 11.5 expected, at +1.56 units (was 7 of 22, 8.3 expected, +0.48 units; 3 of 7 hit this week). A few hits swing the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
College.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
College.evidence: Season: 22 of 24 hit against 21.5 expected, at +0.32 units (was 17 of 19; 5 of 5 this week). Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season.
College.evidence: Season (234 games): average spread miss 12.5 points for the model against 11.9 for Vegas, still a 0.6 gap. Winners right in 154 of 234 (66%), spread record 111-117-4. In the 40 Week 10 results shown: 24 of 39 winners and 17-23 against the spread.
College.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.

College.lesson: The idea that the model's margin runs well above Vegas's when a starting QB is out was not supported by this week's results.
College.evidence: Kansas State (Week 9) fit the idea: model +9.1 vs Vegas +2.5, lost. But in three flagged Week 10 games the model was closer than Vegas each time: Boise State 64-38 (model by 24.5, Vegas 19.5, actual 26), Oklahoma 23-7 over Florida (model Florida by 2.3, Vegas 5.5, 18.3 vs 21.5 off) and Air Force 24-21 over Army (7.0 vs 8.5 off). 1 of 4 supports it.
College.test: On past seasons, flag games where a team's starting QB was out and compare the model's margin error and the Vegas error in those games with all other games. Need 20+ such games.
